scrutiny.failureCase: Polishing a surface without moving the purpose. docs/IDEA.md names zero-friction daily consumption that works offline, and README.md:77 promises a mobile-friendly web briefing; today the detail panel shows raw ## and ** (index.html:2041), so the web reader is worse than the TUI at its one job. Rendering it advances that directly, with vendored files keeping it offline.

Adding a second static-serving pattern or restating a rule the owner already states. api.py:1846 owns the StaticFiles mount pattern and is followed; constitution.md:112 (local-first) is honoured by vendoring rather than a CDN.

Claiming the pipeline renders real summaries from a hand-built fixture. Ran the pinned marked 18.0.14 and DOMPurify 3.4.16 in Chromium over the newest real reading summary and synthesis pulled from cerebro's database: headings, lists and bold rendered as h2, ul/li and strong.
Inserting model output over third-party articles as HTML opens script injection on a page holding the API key in localStorage. Probe in Chromium: marked alone passes
A second markdown renderer beside renderSimpleMarkdown. The design deletes renderSimpleMarkdown (index.html:2068) and routes both fields through one renderMarkdown; the mount follows api.py:1846.
Only seeded fixtures prove rendering. The cerebro probe above ran real stored output; after the build, opening an item on cerebro's web view is the live check.

Assuming the UMD build exposes the globals, that StaticFiles serves .js as JavaScript, or that gitleaks passes minified code. Verified: the probe read typeof marked.parse === 'function' and DOMPurify.version === '3.4.16'; mimetypes.guess_type('a.js') is text/javascript; the repo's gitleaks config over both files reported no leaks.

Missing a consumer of what changes. Enumerated with grep for renderSimpleMarkdown, detail-summary, detail-synthesis h4, synthesis-body and /assets over py, html, md, go, yml and json: the web consumers are index.html and the overflow test at test_web_browser_integration.py:556 (in the design); the TUI's renderSimpleMarkdown is a separate Go function; docs/architecture/components.md:101 describes the web view as 'no framework, no build step', which still holds, and the architecture refresh updates that file.
A runtime filter where structure could forbid it. The tag allowlist makes img, media, svg and script unrepresentable in the output rather than filtering bad attributes after the fact.

A vendored file silently swapped or bumped without its record. VENDORED.json plus a test that hashes each file and checks its banner names the recorded version holds that; what still needs a human is noticing a DOMPurify advisory, since dependabot cannot see vendored files. Accepted out loud as a sacrifice.
A one-way change. The work is files plus one mount; a revert of the commit undoes it with no data or schema change.

Fixing the detail summary while a sibling surface still shows raw model markdown. Swept index.html's innerHTML and escapeHtml sites: feed and must-read cards show the short summary, which summarizer.py:371 asks for as a brief plain summary, and quotes are plain sentences; only reading_summary and synthesis are markdown. Stacks: the fix is JS in the web view; the Go TUI already renders markdown with its own renderer; Python only serves the files; no Rust or JS package units exist. Engines do not apply to product code.
A state or setting the problem does not force. None added: no flag, no fallback path, no renderer toggle.
Two renderers or two records of a version. One renderer replaces the old one; the version in VENDORED.json and the file banner are tied by the banner test.
'Never load third-party resources' living only in a comment. It lives in the allowlist and is asserted by the hostile-summary test's blocked-host check.
No model decides anything at runtime here; rendering is deterministic code.
Restating the overflow or local-first rules. The design extends the existing overflow test and points at constitution.md:112 rather than restating it.

Deciding by matching text. The title rule as recorded compares model output against the stored title; that comparison misses rewrites, and the operator's new rule reads the token's type and depth instead of its text.
Patching around raw markdown with more regex rules in renderSimpleMarkdown. The cause is that the page has no markdown renderer; the design adds one and deletes the partial one.
Guessing what summaries look like from the prompt. Queried cerebro: 498 of the 500 newest reading summaries open with '# <title>', and the six sampled equal the stored title verbatim.

Walked cerebro's 500 newest reading summaries through marked's lexer: 497 open with an h1, all of them the article title or the model's rewrite of it. The exact-equality drop leaves 36 duplicates and a case- and quote-normalized match leaves 20, each a rewrite still shown under the real title. The operator chose to drop the leading h1 unconditionally, which reopens the form.

decisions.question: Exact equality drops 461 of 497 leading-h1 titles, normalized equality 477, and the remaining 20 are model rewrites still shown twice; which rule ships: always drop the leading h1, normalized match, or exact match?
decisions.answer: Always drop the reading summary's leading h1, matched or not; any later h1 still renders.

carried: Should the reading summary's leading h1 be dropped unconditionally rather than only when it equals the article title?
